caseno:
Appeal from Original Order (FMA) No. 34 of 2004 
with Civil Rule No. 736 (FM) of 2003.
lawyer:
Morshed Ahmed Khan, Advocate—For the Appellant. 
Shamim Khaled Ahmed, Advocate—For Respondent No. 1. 
Ozair Farook with SK Md Morshed Advocates—For Respondent No. 15.
parties:
Arab Bangladesh Bank Ltd ------ Appellant
Vs. 
Janata Bank and ors ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Abdur Rashid J: Arab Bank Bangladesh Limited, in short, AB Bank, presented the appeal against order No.44 dated 1-12-03 passed by Artha Rin Adalat No. 4 at Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 41 of 2003, which rejected prayers for transfer of the case and release of the suit property from attachment. 

 2. It appears from the record that AB Bank instituted Title Suit No. 125 of 1992 in the Third Artha Rin Adalat at Dhaka and obtained a preliminary decree on 29-7-99 for Taka 87,79,388 as was due on 30-6-92. The decree was made final on 14-8-2000. Then, on 25-3-2001, AB Bank levied the decree in Title Execution Case No. 38 of 2001 in the same Artha Rin Adalat for realisation of Taka 4,18,65,415. 

 3. In execution, the property of one SB Zaman, which was already mortgaged to AB Bank, was attached. On or about 6-11-03 respondent No. 1 Janata Bank made an application under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure for release of the property from attachment. The application was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 80 of 2003. On further prayer of Janata Bank, the Third Artha Rin Adalat stayed further proceeding of the execution case by an order passed on same date. 

 4. Respondent No. 1 Janata Bank also instituted Title Suit 217 of 1933 in the Fourth Artha Rin Adalat at Dhaka and obtained a preliminary decree on 5-9-99 for Taka 1,14,65,356 as was due on 30-9-93. On 17-7-2000 the decree was made final. Then, Janata Bank on 23-11-2000 started Title Execution Case No.150 of 2000 for realisation of Taka 2,59,49,528. In execution, Janata Bank also got attached very same property which was already mortgaged to it. The execution case was then renumbered as Title Execution Case No. 1210 of 2003. 

 5. Having come to know of such execution, on 19-11-2003. AB Bank made an application under Order XXII, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure in Title Execution Case No. 1210 of 2003 for release of the property from attachment and said application was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 41 of 2003. The Fourth Artha Rin Adalat ultimately, fixed 1-12-03 for hearing on maintainability of the application. On the date, AB Bank also filed an application for an order for analogous hearing of the miscellaneous case with that of the Third Artha Rin Adalat. 

 8. He however submitted that on the very same date, 1-12-2003, AB Bank made an application under section 27(1) read with section of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (Act VIII of 2003), hereinafter referred as the Ain, in Title Execution Case No. 38 of 2001 of Third Artha Rin Adalat for sending its decree to the Fourth Artha Rin Adalat for execution. But Third Artha Rin Adalat rejected the application by an order passed on the same date. 

 11. In the circumstances, he submitted the Fourth Artha Rin Adalat did not commit any error in rejecting the misconceived applications of the appellant either for analogous hearing of miscellaneous case or for release of the property from attachment. 

 13. From the above facts, one thing becomes clear that two execution cases are now pending in two Artha Rin Adalats, namely, Third Artha Rain Adalat and Fourth Artha Rin Adalat at Dhaka, against the same property of SB Zaman which was also attached by both Adalats. Both Adalats appear to have got equal jurisdiction. Janata Bank already obtained stay of further proceedings in Miscellaneous Case No. 38 of 2003 of Third Artha Rin Adalat and started proceeding a bit fast with its own execution case in Fourth Artha Rin Adalat. 

 14. Consequently, in Miscellaneous Case 1210 of 2003, AB Bank made an application under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure before Fourth Artha Rin Adalat for release of the property from attachment. Fourth Artha Rin Adalat posted the application for hearing on maintainability on 1-12-2003, the closing day of civil Courts before civil vacation. AB Bank also made another application for analogous hearing of its Miscellaneous Case No. 80 of 2003 pending before Third Artha Rin Adalat with that of Janata Bank. 

 15. As stated, Fourth Artha Rin Adalat rejected both prayers. We understand the order rejecting the prayer for analogous hearing of the Miscellaneous Cases pending before two Artha Rin Adalats. But we failed to persuade ourselves to accept ultimate decision of the Third Artha Rin Adalat in rejecting the objection and claim of AB Bank, summarily. 

 19. When two execution cases are proceeding in two different Artha Rin Adalats, under section 27(1) of the Ain, one of the Adalats, either on its motion or on the application of decree holder, should send the decree to other Adalat, for execution. On the very same date, AB Bank made an application under section 27(1) of the Ain in Third Artha Rin Adalat for sending the decree to Fourth Artha Rin Adalat but Third Artha Rin Adalat without understanding intention of the legislature rejected the application. Against such order, if AB Bank would have proceeded up it would not have faced the present predicament. 

 21. We would have been happy to stop here, had we been satisfied that unwanted situation arisen out of continuance of two execution proceedings in two Artha Rin Adalats against the same attached property has been set at rest by the impugned order. In the facts and circumstances of the case and in. the interest of justice, it is our considered view that Fourth Artha Rin Adalat which now holds the property must dispose of both execution cases under section 27 of the Ain.
